issue.title: Full-history agent load is ~1x source scan on warm archives: shared per-row Python decode dominates both paths
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-zu.8.5 (epic sase-zu.8, acceptance) as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #2; filed by sase-zu.8.land on 2026-09-13. Not caused by sase-zu.8: the per-row Python decode cost predates the epic and dominates the source-scan path equally.

A single non-selective full-history Agents load is ~1x a full source scan on the warm 13k synthetic fixture (sase-zu.8.5 acceptance, master ef254fd6dc: production full history 9281 ms p50 vs source 8933 ms, 0.96x). Stage attribution shows shared per-row Python work dominates both paths: dict-to-wire conversion ~1.3 s, Agent decode ~2.0 s, agents-live field entries ~2.9 s; the epic's revalidate adds ~660 ms Rust (source reconcile plus 12,938 marker signatures).

The index still wins everywhere else (bounded first paint 88x, 10-refresh session 10.6x synthetic / 12.6x athena, athena full history 3.64x because real source scanning is slower), so this bounds only the one-shot warm full-history path.

Remediation candidates from the acceptance run: retain decoded rows keyed by marker signature, lazy decode, or skip hidden-row marker repair already covered by the source-reconcile pass (that last overlaps sase-vc's hidden-row repair work — coordinate, do not duplicate). Needs a planning pass to choose among them; retention keyed by marker signature would cross the Rust core boundary.

task_type_fields.impact: One-shot warm full-history loads get no speedup from the artifact index; bounded first paint (88x) and settled sessions (10.6-12.6x) are unaffected.
